title: Tech Note: Google Calendar: Downloading Future Events
author: Robert Molina, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note demonstrates integrating 4D with Google Calendar's original GData/REST API using raw HTTP requests built and parsed manually via 4D Internet Commands, since no 4D-specific client library existed. It is now obsolete in a very concrete way: Google's ClientLogin authentication (plaintext username/password POST) was deprecated and shut down years ago in favor of OAuth 2.0, and the GData protocol itself was replaced by Google Calendar API v3 (JSON/REST), so none of the endpoints or request formats shown will function today. The underlying pattern — building raw HTTP requests and parsing XML/JSON responses from 4D to talk to a REST web service — remains a valid and still-used integration technique, just with 4D's more modern HTTP and JSON commands instead of manual request-string construction.
related_updates: Google's ClientLogin authentication mechanism was deprecated and discontinued in favor of OAuth 2.0
The GData-based Google Calendar API described here was replaced by the newer Google Calendar API (JSON/REST, OAuth-based)
4D has since added more built-in HTTP client and JSON commands, reducing the need for manual raw HTTP request construction shown in this note
